planning_note: Calendar forecasts use the user-selected September 4 start and a 20:00 EDT planning reference. Original planning_window values preserve the proposal; schedule dates and elapsed hours are the reviewed forecast. Human assignments and actual kickoff remain unconfirmed.

tasks.title: Current reproducible baseline
tasks.outcome: An identified current source can be reproduced, inspected, and measured without changing user projects.
tasks.scope: Coordinate R00, R02, R03, and conditional R04; retain failures and unavailable native capabilities as explicit evidence.
acceptance: Fresh-checkout CPU checks and named baseline commands run against an identified source revision.
Native, browser, and packaged-desktop results are reported separately as pass, fail, blocked, or not run.
The baseline records source, build, fixture, platform, and limitation evidence without treating historical counts as current proof.

schedule.rationale: Rolls up R00/R02/R03 and conditional R04 baseline work.

tasks.title: Portable rules and enforceable boundaries
tasks.outcome: Contributors share enforceable architecture, isolation, task, and CI rules from a clean clone.
tasks.scope: Coordinate R01 and R05-R07, including instruction portability, module policies, isolated execution, and real gate preparation.
acceptance: A clean clone finds the adopted instructions and task/receipt contract.
Deliberate dependency, size, schema, and isolation violations fail with useful diagnostics.
Required-check configuration is proposed only after the named workflows exist and report missing required jobs as failures.

schedule.rationale: Rolls up portable rules, module gates, isolation, and CI preparation; independent prep overlaps F0.

tasks.title: Contracts, first extraction, and diagnostics
tasks.outcome: One migrated aggregate has explicit ownership, commands, history, diagnostics, and independently checked replay.
tasks.scope: Coordinate R08-R12 across animation extraction, foundational contracts, native feasibility, transactions, and deterministic diagnostics.
acceptance: One aggregate has one writable authority and a documented cutover and rollback path.
One gesture produces one undo action; stale and duplicate writes fail according to declared semantics.
A real application caller uses the extracted seam and deterministic replay matches an independent expectation.

schedule.rationale: Rolls up extraction, contracts, commands, diagnostics, and native feasibility after their task prerequisites.

tasks.title: Complete slice, Rust MCP, and native effect
tasks.outcome: A representative property, second command shape, Rust MCP path, native effect, and precision boundary work through shared services.
tasks.scope: Coordinate R13-R17 while preserving one state authority and explicit native/browser capability differences.
acceptance: UI, SDK, direct API, and both MCP clients reach equivalent accepted outcomes on identified builds.
The property and plugin survive relevant keying, undo/redo, save/reload, render/export, cancellation, absence, and fault cases.
Browser and packaged-desktop evidence are separate, and native support is established only on the packaged artifact.

schedule.rationale: Initial property and MCP proof reach H24; gesture, color, and real native effect continue afterward.

tasks.title: All shipped subsystem migrations
tasks.outcome: Every shipped subsystem is migrated through bounded family issues or carries an explicit maintainer-approved exception.
tasks.scope: Coordinate the R18 epic and its six dependency-ordered families; keep inventory, capability, consumer, evidence, and legacy-retirement state visible.
acceptance: Every shipped actionable surface is mapped to a capability and handler or an explicit owned exception.
Persistent state covers document, save/load, undo/redo, selection, animation, render, export, and native bridges wherever applicable.
Each family has independent behavior evidence; generated coverage and file-size reduction are supporting evidence only.

schedule.rationale: Rolls up the six R18 families as accepted interfaces make each family ready.

tasks.title: Performance, resilience, and distribution
tasks.outcome: Measured workloads, recovery cases, and supported distribution paths pass on identified artifacts.
tasks.scope: Coordinate R19-R21 across controlled performance, fault recovery, generated artifacts, sidecars, media, plugins, desktop packages, and supported operating systems.
acceptance: Budgets derive from controlled product fixtures and include output-equivalence checks.
Required recovery and interruption cases pass or remain visible blockers with owners and next actions.
Browser, packaged desktop, media/export, native plugin, and supported-OS evidence identify exact bytes and do not substitute for one another.

schedule.rationale: Continuous measurement begins early; recovery and packaged validation finish after migrations converge.

tasks.title: Close foundation remediation
tasks.outcome: The identified integrated candidate satisfies the full foundation close gate and receives maintainer acceptance.
tasks.scope: Coordinate R22 inventory reconciliation, bypass retirement, clean-clone and fresh-agent rehearsal, current browser/desktop evidence, and final acceptance.
acceptance: No shipped actionable surface, persistent-data consumer, or writable bypass remains unowned or silently unmapped.
Clean-clone Codex and Claude sessions use the same adopted instructions and complete a bounded task through the current protocol.
The maintainer accepts the identified candidate and artifacts; merged code, green unit tests, or agent receipts alone do not close the epic.

schedule.rationale: R22 targets H240; the phase remains open through the explicit H240-H336 acceptance buffer.

tasks.title: Resolve kickoff baseline and active work
tasks.outcome: Kickoff has one current base, reconciled active work, explicit supported-platform candidates, and no conflicting writer scopes.
tasks.scope: Refresh main and open work; collect branches, heads, dirty/unpushed state, paths, contracts, sessions, and next checkpoints; identify the integration-owner and backup decisions still required.
acceptance: Current main, active PRs, local work, and collision candidates are recorded from a fresh read.
Every proposed writer scope has a base, branch/worktree, exact paths, dependencies, and next checkpoint.
No assignment, platform commitment, or authority is inferred where the maintainer has not supplied it.

schedule.rationale: Resolve current source, active work, ownership decisions, and collisions before dependent tasks.

tasks.title: Adopt portable handbook and work tracking
tasks.outcome: A clean clone exposes concise shared rules, task packets, receipts, and canonical work tracking without private local context.
tasks.scope: Adopt the reviewed handbook, short Codex/Claude entry points, issue/receipt templates, GitHub Project proposal, and current dedicated-workspace collaboration contract.
acceptance: A fresh contributor can locate the same architecture, quality, authority, and task instructions.
Ready-item bodies carry outcome, scope, dependencies, acceptance, base/worktree, evidence, and authority fields.
Private local notes, credentials, machine paths, and obsolete manual-grant onboarding are absent from shared guidance.

schedule.rationale: Begins after R00 and BZ0 establish the current authority contract.

tasks.title: Add reproducible commands, doctor, and receipts
tasks.outcome: Developers can identify source/build state, inspect prerequisites, and run named checks that emit structured results.
tasks.scope: Add read-only doctor behavior, source/build identity, named check/test/browser/desktop/build/package commands, and per-run receipts with explicit unavailable states.
acceptance: Doctor reports prerequisites and capabilities without mutating the workstation or project.
Commands record source, build, platform, fixture, pass/fail/blocked/not-run, artifacts, and limitations.
A missing native or GPU environment remains blocked and cannot be converted to a passing skip.

schedule.rationale: Baseline commands and receipts proceed immediately after the source is selected.

tasks.title: Inventory surfaces, consumers, fixtures, and workloads
tasks.outcome: Nemo has an actionable surface-to-capability inventory, deterministic fixture corpus, and initial measured workloads.
tasks.scope: Catalog visible, contextual, dynamic, modal, canvas, plugin, preference, and external-service operations plus every applicable document, save/load, undo/redo, selection, animation, render, export, and native-bridge consumer.
acceptance: Each inventory row maps surface, capability, handler, UI/SDK/MCP exposure, consumers, fixtures, platforms, status, and next gate.
Fixtures cover static/keyed/expression properties, held frames, components, masks/alpha, text, mesh, media, migration, interaction, and export with independent expectations.
Initial evaluation, render, copy, memory, and export measurements identify workload, hardware, backend, and source revision without inventing budgets.

schedule.rationale: Surface inventory and initial fixtures run in parallel with baseline command work.

tasks.title: Repair reproduced native sidecar packaging blockers
tasks.outcome: Any native or sidecar blocker reproduced on the selected base is repaired and packaged reproducibly, or the conditional task closes with non-reproduction evidence.
tasks.scope: Reproduce current FFmpeg/Theora and sidecar prerequisites on the selected base; repair only confirmed blockers while preserving codec, dependency, and distribution policy.
acceptance: The blocker is reproduced on an identified base and packaged build before implementation, or non-reproduction is documented with environment evidence.
The packaged artifact includes or locates the approved dependency without relying on an undocumented workstation installation.
Actual packaged-desktop launch and affected media/export behavior pass; browser checks are recorded separately.

schedule.rationale: Conditional slot for a blocker reproduced by R02; non-reproduction yields evidence rather than repair work.

tasks.title: Enforce module profiles and dependency boundaries
tasks.outcome: Architecture checks prevent new cycles, forbidden edges, implicit globals, unreviewed size growth, and stale exceptions.
tasks.scope: Profile every source file; define public API, owner, lifecycle, dependencies, fixtures, and performance invariants; install exact-path debt and exception checks.
acceptance: Every handwritten source file has a reviewed profile or explicit generated/vendor/data policy.
Deliberate cycle, private import, global-state, size, and exception violations fail the same checks used by CI.
Legacy ceilings can shrink but cannot silently grow; exceptions name path, rule, reason, owner, issue, and review point.

schedule.rationale: Portable rules and the surface inventory provide the inputs for enforceable profiles.

tasks.title: Isolate task runtimes and mutable artifacts
tasks.outcome: Concurrent tasks cannot overwrite one another's source state, browser data, desktop data, ports, caches, builds, or reports.
tasks.scope: Provide task-specific worktrees, launcher identity, ports, browser contexts/origins, Tauri data roots, temp/cache/output paths, build products, reports, and serialized desktop/GPU slots.
acceptance: Two task instances run concurrently with distinct browser, Tauri, temp, cache, build, and report state.
Each process exposes a source/build handshake and only its owner can stop it.
Shared desktop input and reference GPU measurements use explicit exclusive reservations.

schedule.rationale: Starts when R02 has named commands and source/build identities to isolate.

tasks.title: Install real PR and CI gates
tasks.outcome: Candidate changes run reproducible static, behavior, browser, native, and build gates appropriate to their affected surfaces.
tasks.scope: Create actual workflows and stable aggregate reporting; validate names and failure semantics before an authorized owner configures required checks and review policy.
acceptance: The candidate runs static/architecture, CPU, document-contract, affected-browser, and required native/build jobs through the same scripts used locally.
Missing, cancelled, or unavailable required work reports failure or blocked status rather than success.
Credentialed Project/repository settings remain separate from untrusted pull-request execution and are changed only by authorized owners.

schedule.rationale: CI gates start after commands, module checks, and isolation are executable.

tasks.title: Extract a pure animation seam and select a runner
tasks.outcome: One pure animation/easing module runs through a compatibility facade in production, with an evidence-based Node-or-Vitest decision.
tasks.scope: Characterize and extract one easing/interpolation seam; compare Node and Vitest on the same pure unit, stateful behavior, browser control, source maps, setup, speed, and worktree isolation.
acceptance: The real application imports the extracted module through a bounded facade and preserves characterized output.
Node and Vitest exercise the same meaningful expectations; duplicated long-term suites are not retained.
An ADR records the selected runner, type-check boundary, diagnostics, performance, and rejected alternatives.

schedule.rationale: The characterized surface, profiles, and isolated runner allow a bounded extraction trial.

tasks.title: Define foundational ownership and data contracts
tasks.outcome: Stable IDs, state authority, time, persistence, image/color, platform capability, and dependency direction are versioned contracts with generated boundary types.
tasks.scope: Define persistent versus transient and derived state, exact ownership transitions, precise time, image precision/color/alpha, schema compatibility, platform availability, and native/WASM ports.
acceptance: Each migrated aggregate names one writer, all read/write paths, serialization/history ownership, cutover, rollback, and unknown-data policy.
Stable IDs and supported fields survive create/edit/key/undo/redo/reorder/duplicate/save/load and relevant selection, animation, render, export, and native consumers.
Generated Rust/TypeScript/schema artifacts are versioned and drift checks fail when source contracts disagree.

schedule.rationale: Foundational contracts start when rules, inventory, and architecture gates converge.

tasks.title: Prove native OpenFX feasibility
tasks.outcome: A disposable prototype proves or falsifies the selected native OpenFX load, describe, and CPU float-render boundary.
tasks.scope: Use the accepted image/parameter port to test plugin discovery, describe, buffer ownership, render, lifecycle, licensing, and platform prerequisites without creating a second product backend.
acceptance: A redistributable test plugin loads, describes supported parameters, and renders a known float fixture on an identified native environment.
Buffer ownership, precision, lifecycle, failure mode, and distribution constraints are recorded.
The prototype is either integrated through the accepted contracts or explicitly retired after the decision.

schedule.rationale: Native feasibility waits for R04 evidence and R09 image/parameter contracts.

tasks.title: Implement commands, transactions, history, and authority cutover
tasks.outcome: One aggregate mutates through shared queries, commands, transactions, gesture lifecycle, history, revision checks, and invalidation.
tasks.scope: Add begin/update/commit/cancel, atomic batch semantics, stable request/document/object IDs, optimistic revisions, idempotency, cancellation, and feature registration without a hand-edited central switch.
acceptance: One gesture commits one undo entry; cancel restores declared state; undo/redo and missing-object cases match independent expectations.
Stale revisions and duplicate requests cannot silently overwrite or double-apply persistent state.
All write paths for the migrated aggregate route through one authority, including UI, history, persistence, animation, render/export, and native adapters where applicable.

schedule.rationale: Dispatcher and history work begins after the ownership contracts land.

tasks.title: Add structured diagnostics and deterministic replay
tasks.outcome: The application, CLI, tests, and future MCP adapter share bounded diagnostics and deterministic fixture record/replay.
tasks.scope: Emit structured source/build/operation/revision IDs, capability state, timings, resource counters, trace bundles, seeds, replay operations, and redaction/size limits.
acceptance: A retained fixture and operation sequence replay to an independently checked result on the identified build.
Diagnostics expose availability, errors, timings, resource state, and artifact references without credentials or unbounded data.
Enabling diagnostics uses the product execution path and does not hide release-only failures.

schedule.rationale: Deterministic diagnostics require isolation, contracts, and a real command/history path.

tasks.title: Migrate one complete animated property
tasks.outcome: A characterized animated property uses one shared handler across inspector, timeline, SDK, persistence, evaluation, and output.
tasks.scope: Use opacity or another approved representative property; preserve static/keyed/expression/nested-context semantics and units while removing direct mutation bypasses for that surface.
acceptance: Create/edit/key/frame-change/undo/redo/save/reopen and nested-context behavior match declared expectations.
Selection and animation state remain correct, and browser render plus export output are checked independently.
UI, SDK, and direct API reach the same command result with one writable authority and no remaining surface-specific setter.

schedule.rationale: The first property slice starts after extraction, commands, and replay diagnostics finish.

tasks.title: Add Rust MCP adapter and two-client parity
tasks.outcome: A thin Rust MCP adapter exposes shared discovery, queries, commands, jobs, and diagnostics to Codex and Claude.
tasks.scope: Keep transport outside domain/application modules; pin protocol behavior; identify instance/build/document/revision/request/job; support runtime, diagnostic, and explicitly enabled developer-workspace modes.
acceptance: Codex and Claude discover the same capabilities and produce outcomes equivalent to direct application API calls.
Reconnect, cancellation, stale-write, idempotency, pagination/list-change, and intended-instance attachment cases pass.
Pixels and geometry do not travel through command JSON, and release runtime authority is distinct from source-workspace authority.

schedule.rationale: Initial Rust MCP and two-client proof consumes the completed property and shared services.

tasks.title: Prove a gesture or asynchronous job slice
tasks.outcome: The shared contract handles a non-scalar interaction through a geometric gesture or asynchronous export job.
tasks.scope: Implement begin/update/commit/cancel with coordinate/sample semantics, or a progress/cancel export job with immutable input revision and artifact result; route UI/API/MCP consumers.
acceptance: Commit creates one history action and cancel restores state, or the job reports progress and cancellation without publishing a partial result as complete.
Stale revisions, late results, disconnects, and retries follow declared behavior.
The actual UI interaction and direct API/MCP paths are each exercised; correct core logic cannot mask broken bindings.

schedule.rationale: The second command shape follows accepted property and MCP seams.

tasks.title: Integrate one redistributable OpenFX effect
tasks.outcome: One real redistributable OpenFX effect works through the registry, UI, application API, and MCP on supported native builds.
tasks.scope: Implement descriptor mapping, keyable parameters, thread-safety, temporal dependencies, cache invalidation, process lifecycle, cancellation, timeouts, missing-plugin persistence, and host-fault containment.
acceptance: The effect can be add/edit/key/undo/redo/save/reload/rendered through UI and MCP with known-frame output checks.
Missing plugin, cancellation, timeout, and host crash preserve document IDs and parameters and do not corrupt the project.
Packaged native evidence records supported suites, contexts, platforms, and limits; browser reports unavailable or explicitly baked behavior.

schedule.rationale: Real effect integration starts after feasibility, property/MCP, and R17 color contracts; full plugin proof is post-H24.

tasks.title: Prove color, precision, EXR, and OTIO boundaries
tasks.outcome: Color transforms, half/float image handling, EXR fixtures, and an explicit OTIO subset/loss contract establish the native image boundary.
tasks.scope: Define precision, alpha, color space, transforms, buffer ownership, native document-format preservation, and precise time/media-reference interchange without silently clamping to RGBA8.
acceptance: Small OCIO/EXR fixtures demonstrate declared transforms, alpha, precision, and round-trip limits.
OTIO import/export reports the supported subset and every lossy or unsupported construct explicitly.
Browser and desktop capability differences are explicit, and shared image contracts land before R16 consumers depend on them.

schedule.rationale: Color, precision, EXR, and OTIO proof begins after R09 and R10 and lands before R16.

tasks.title: Coordinate all shipped subsystem migrations
tasks.outcome: Six bounded migration families retire legacy writers while preserving every shipped surface and relevant consumer.
tasks.scope: Maintain the capability/module inventory and coordinate R18.1-R18.6 through characterize, facade, consumer routing, behavior proof, integration, old-writer removal, and documentation updates.
acceptance: Each child family reaches migrated and validated state or records an explicit maintainer-approved exception.
No family closes on registry counts, generated tests, or line counts without direct behavior and data-preservation evidence.
The integrated inventory identifies authority, readers/writers, fixtures, platforms, MCP exposure, debt, and next gate for every row.

schedule.rationale: Rolls up R18.1-R18.6; H20-H36 is justified family prep before the R15 coordination acceptance dependency clears.

tasks.title: Migrate document identity, codecs, recovery, components, and history
tasks.outcome: Document identity, serialization, recovery, components, and history use one authority and preserve supported project data.
tasks.scope: Migrate stable IDs, format codecs/migrations, unknown fields, linked/embedded assets, component scope, atomic save/recovery, transactions, and undo/redo behind compatible facades.
acceptance: Create/edit/key/reorder/duplicate/group/undo/redo/save/load and recovery preserve stable IDs, supported fields, assets, components, and unknown-data policy.
Selection, animation evaluation, render/export, and native bridges consume the same document identity and revision rules where applicable.
Old/current/damaged/newer-schema fixtures prove explicit migration, recovery, refusal, or loss-report behavior before the old writer is removed.

schedule.rationale: Document migration can begin after R09/R11/R13 without waiting for unrelated gesture or native-effect work.

tasks.title: Migrate time, tracks, easing, expressions, parenting, and timeline
tasks.outcome: Animation and timeline semantics use precise shared time and deterministic evaluation across nested contexts.
tasks.scope: Migrate tracks, keyed/held frames, easing, expressions, parenting, component timing, dependency/cycle policy, deterministic randomness, timeline model, play/pause, and scrub behavior.
acceptance: Static/keyed/held/expression/parented/nested fixtures match independent expectations across edit, undo/redo, save/load, and frame evaluation.
Selection and playhead are not mutated by headless evaluation; render/export sample the same declared time semantics.
UI/API/MCP timeline operations reach shared handlers, and legacy animation writers are retired after parity evidence.

schedule.rationale: Animation/timeline migration waits for the document identity/history family.

tasks.title: Migrate render graph, masks, effects, color resources, caches, and scheduler
tasks.outcome: Rendering evaluates immutable revisions through explicit graph, resource, cache, and scheduling contracts.
tasks.scope: Migrate render graph, masks/effects, retained IDs, typed bulk data, precision/alpha/color resources, cache keys/invalidation, scheduling, device loss, and native/WASM adapters.
acceptance: Representative masks, alpha, effects, text, mesh, temporal, and nested fixtures match declared output across browser render and export.
Edits, keying, undo/redo, save/load, and selection invalidation reach the same revision-based render inputs without mutating live Paper state.
Native/WASM parity and differences are fixture-backed; device loss, cache invalidation, and resource ownership have explicit recovery behavior.

schedule.rationale: Renderer migration runs beside R18.2 after document and color prerequisites land.

tasks.title: Migrate drawing, selection, gestures, inspectors, timeline UI, text, rig, and mesh
tasks.outcome: Editor tools and controls use shared capabilities and gesture semantics without direct persistent-state mutation.
tasks.scope: Migrate drawing, hit testing, selection, geometric gestures, inspector, graph/timeline controls, text, rig, mesh, contextual controls, workspaces, and native dialog/job counterparts.
acceptance: Representative create/select/edit/drag/key/undo/redo/save/reload workflows preserve selection, document, animation, and history semantics.
Browser interactions and packaged-desktop/native-dialog paths are exercised separately where each exists.
UI, SDK, and MCP capability mappings cover visible, contextual, modal, and dynamic controls; presentation-only state is explicitly classified.

schedule.rationale: Editor tools follow gesture, document, and animation/timeline foundations.

tasks.title: Migrate media, import/export, OpenFX, extensions, and service adapters
tasks.outcome: Media, interchange, plugins, extensions, and external services use explicit ports, capabilities, persistence, and fault boundaries.
tasks.scope: Migrate media/proxies/audio as supported, asset references, import/export, codecs, OpenFX/extensions, external authentication adapters, cancellation, and packaged sidecars.
acceptance: Import/edit/key/undo/redo/save/reload/render/export/reimport preserve supported media, effect parameters, IDs, references, and declared loss behavior.
Missing assets/plugins, auth denial, cancellation, timeout, and host/worker failure preserve the document and report actionable diagnostics.
Actual packaged desktop proves native plugin/media paths; browser behavior reports explicit availability or baked fallback and is validated separately.

schedule.rationale: Media/export/native adapters follow the real effect, color, document, and renderer families.

tasks.title: Migrate preferences, shortcuts, dynamic controls, diagnostics, and Labs
tasks.outcome: Application settings, shortcuts, dynamic surfaces, diagnostics, and experimental features have explicit ownership and disposition.
tasks.scope: Migrate preference and UI-state persistence, shortcut dispatch, contextual/dynamic registry controls, diagnostics surfaces, workspaces, and Labs items with promote, retain-experimental, or retire decisions.
acceptance: Preference and UI-session operations declare persistence and undo semantics separately from document commands.
Shortcut, contextual, and dynamic plugin controls map to shared handlers or explicit presentation-only/unavailable states across UI/API/MCP.
Every Labs surface has a maintainer-approved disposition and evidence; clean restart and packaged-desktop behavior are checked where applicable.

schedule.rationale: Preferences, dynamic controls, diagnostics, and Labs follow the migrated editor-control family.

tasks.title: Set workload budgets and run performance/soak regressions
tasks.outcome: Agreed latency, throughput, memory, cache, copy, export, and soak budgets are enforced against representative fixtures.
tasks.scope: Expand baseline workloads to complex scenes, temporal effects, large media, long sessions, and export; measure p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU completion, memory plateau, cache pressure, copies, cancellation, and throughput.
acceptance: Budgets identify fixture, source/artifact, hardware, backend/driver, warm/cold state, repetitions, and statistical summary.
Performance comparisons also verify declared visual/numeric output equivalence.
Regressions fail with retained evidence; missing reference hardware remains visible rather than becoming a passing claim.

schedule.rationale: Measurement starts from R03/R12 and expands continuously as migration candidates integrate.

tasks.title: Exercise recovery, fault, and migration behavior
tasks.outcome: Document and job state recover predictably from interruption, damage, missing dependencies, crashes, device loss, stale sessions, disconnects, and disk failures.
tasks.scope: Run fault scenarios for save/load/migration, assets/plugins, worker/host/device/process failure, job cancellation/reconnect, disk exhaustion, and restart; preserve minimized seeds and recovery artifacts.
acceptance: Interrupted saves and old/damaged/newer documents preserve prior recoverable data and follow explicit migration, refusal, or recovery policy.
Missing assets/plugins, crashes, device loss, stale clients, disconnects, and disk failure cannot apply late or duplicate writes to a newer revision.
Recovered documents retain IDs, fields, selection-relevant identity, animation data, render/export inputs, and native references where applicable.

schedule.rationale: Full recovery/fault acceptance starts when all named migration-family dependencies finish.

tasks.title: Validate generated, native, browser, and packaged distribution
tasks.outcome: Generated WASM, sidecars, plugins, media export/reimport, installed desktop artifacts, and each claimed operating system are validated on identified bytes.
tasks.scope: Regenerate and serve WASM, reproduce sidecars, load plugins, export/reimport representative media, launch installed packages, and run support-matrix checks through the reviewed signing/update path.
acceptance: The served browser build proves browser behavior and capability reporting on its own artifact.
The installed packaged desktop proves native sidecar, plugin, filesystem, media/export, and recovery paths on its own artifact.
Unsupported or untested operating systems remain explicit blockers to only the corresponding support claim.

schedule.rationale: Packaged/browser/OS validation follows native, media, performance, and recovery evidence.

tasks.title: Reconcile inventory and obtain foundation acceptance
tasks.outcome: The full shipped surface inventory, architecture, evidence, onboarding, and release path agree with an accepted integrated candidate.
tasks.scope: Reconcile capability coverage, retire obsolete globals/adapters/flags, enforce boundaries, run clean-clone and fresh-agent rehearsals, validate both clients and platforms, update public guidance, and request maintainer acceptance.
acceptance: Every actionable surface and persistent consumer is migrated, explicitly unavailable, or covered by an owned maintainer-approved exception; no writable bypass remains.
Current browser and packaged-desktop artifacts pass applicable UI/API/SDK/MCP, save/load, undo/redo, animation, render/export, performance, recovery, and support-matrix gates.
Fresh Codex and Claude sessions complete a bounded task from adopted instructions, and the maintainer accepts the exact candidate/artifacts.

schedule.rationale: Inventory reconciliation and maintainer acceptance target day 10 after all explicit predecessors finish.

tasks.title: Adopt collaboration authority and continuity contract
tasks.outcome: Nemo collaboration uses one current authority, identity, task-continuity, and evidence contract.
tasks.scope: Adopt NEMO-A2A-1, GitHub canonical status, verified identities, sole coordination sequencing, explicit publication/release boundaries, and task preservation; replace obsolete manual-grant assumptions with mandatory automatic dedicated-workspace access.
acceptance: All current instructions describe the dedicated Nemo workspace as automatically supplying project repository access to enrolled collaborators and managed agents.
GitHub remains canonical for source, issues, PRs, CI, and review; Buzz carries conversation and coordination.
Relay storage, processed, accepted, completed, reviewed, merged, deployed, released, and maintainer-accepted states remain distinct.

schedule.rationale: Confirm the current collaboration authority and continuity contract at kickoff.

tasks.title: Verify authenticated desktop onboarding and self-service agents
tasks.outcome: Eligible collaborators join authenticated Buzz Desktop and create owner-backed agents through a one-step self-service flow.
tasks.scope: Verify identity backup, collaborator eligibility, member admission, desktop connection/history, owner-backed agent creation, provider separation, directed response policy, and denial outside authorized channels.
acceptance: A new eligible collaborator connects in the desktop app, sends/replies, relaunches with history, and cannot access an unauthorized channel.
The collaborator creates a distinct owner-backed managed agent without sharing provider credentials or private keys.
Agent response, reconnect, and duplicate-execution checks pass under the automatically supplied dedicated-workspace project access.

schedule.rationale: Remaining desktop onboarding and owner-backed agent checks follow BZ0.

tasks.title: Bind one Nemo Project to the canonical repository
tasks.outcome: One Buzz Project resolves the canonical Nemo GitHub repository and local checkout consistently for enrolled collaborators and managed agents.
tasks.scope: Bind repository identity, origin, home channel, immutable instruction revision, and workspace checkout discovery; rely on the dedicated workspace's automatic full repository access rather than user-maintained peer/path grant forms.
acceptance: Project repository identity and Git origin match https://github.com/mysteropodes/nemo.git on every tested workspace.
Enrolled managed sessions receive the current project instructions and can read/write the Project checkout under ordinary repository protections.
Machine-local roots and credentials remain out of signed events, issue bodies, evidence, and model prompts.

schedule.rationale: Verify the existing Nemo Project/repository binding and automatic workspace access after BZ0.

tasks.title: Validate typed A2A lifecycle, reconnect, handoff, and revocation
tasks.outcome: Typed A2A jobs fail closed and preserve exactly-once ownership semantics across retry, reconnect, cancellation, handoff, revocation, and indeterminate recovery.
tasks.scope: Validate peer discovery, dispatch, processed/accepted ownership, progress/terminal receipts, byte-equivalent retry, cancellation acknowledgement, epoch-based handoff, reconnect reconciliation, and identity revocation using trusted tools.
acceptance: Relay acknowledgement alone cannot claim ownership or completion; processed and accepted receipts precede side effects.
Byte-equivalent retries do not execute twice; changed work uses a new request; crashes without terminal receipt become indeterminate for reconciliation.
Cancellation completes only on cancelled acknowledgement, handoff requires successor acceptance, and revocation denies fresh job and protected-resource access.

schedule.rationale: Run remaining lifecycle, reconnect, handoff, cancellation, and revocation acceptance after onboarding/binding evidence.

tasks.title: Link GitHub issues, PRs, and runs idempotently
tasks.outcome: Buzz coordination links canonical GitHub issues, PRs, reviews, and workflow runs without creating a competing backlog or duplicate effects.
tasks.scope: Implement signed, idempotent allowed-event links and status updates; preserve GitHub canonical records, credential separation, one coordinator for status changes, and Validate state after merge where runtime evidence remains.
acceptance: Replayed GitHub events do not duplicate Project items, links, comments, or status transitions.
Only intentionally triaged items enter the Project, and merged work moves to Validate when desktop/export/runtime evidence remains.
Credentialed GitHub writes are isolated from untrusted pull-request code and retain canonical issue/PR/run identifiers.

schedule.rationale: GitHub link validation waits for BZ3 and executable R07 gates.

tasks.title: Carry CI and product-MCP diagnostic receipts
tasks.outcome: Buzz task state carries tamper-evident links to CI and Nemo product-MCP diagnostic evidence as those capabilities become available.
tasks.scope: Associate source/base/candidate/build IDs, command or interaction, fixture/seed, platform, artifact hashes, result state, limitations, and direct API/MCP parity without embedding large or sensitive artifacts.
acceptance: Receipts distinguish pass, fail, blocked, not run, implemented, observed, and accepted states on exact source/build identities.
CI and product-MCP references resolve to bounded artifacts with hashes and redaction limits; missing required evidence remains visible.
An agent completion message, relay receipt, source change, or historical test count cannot advance the item to Done by itself.

schedule.rationale: CI and product-MCP receipt linking follows BZ3, R07, R12, and the H24 R14 proof.

tasks.title: Prove backup, restore, offboarding, upgrades, and support ownership
tasks.outcome: Private Buzz collaboration can be backed up, restored, upgraded, monitored, supported, and safely offboarded on identified distributed builds.
tasks.scope: Exercise identity/config/data backup and restore, service and desktop upgrades, monitoring, incident/support ownership, agent and human offboarding, grant reconciliation, and preserved work evidence.
acceptance: A documented restore on an identified build recovers required history, Project bindings, and operational state without exposing credentials.
Offboarding revokes sponsored agents before the human, denies fresh WebSocket/protected HTTP/media/job access, and preserves work/evidence for reconciliation.
Final distributed-build live acceptance and release decisions remain with the release-owning session and designated human authority.
